title: Two-Tier Fragrance Layering Set Packaging: A Buyer’s Guide
seoTitle: Two-Tier Fragrance Layering Set Packaging | MTT
summary: Plan a two-tier fragrance gift box for a bottle and vials: compare tray access, insert fit, sample checks and complete-set shipping.
intro: A two-tier fragrance set can place a full-size bottle and smaller vials in separate trays while keeping one coordinated gift box. Start with the filled products, then decide which layer the recipient sees first, how each tray is lifted and where the lid clears the contents. Check the assembled set and its shipping pack with physical samples.
cta: Send the filled bottle and vial dimensions, weights, product drawings, intended presentation sequence, quantity per design and delivery country. MTT can review the structure, insert options and sampling brief for a project of 1,000 pieces per design or more.
sections: Start with the complete fragrance set

The pictured fragrance layering set is a design reference: it shows a full-size bottle with a separate vial presentation and a decorated lift-off cover. It is a useful starting point for discussing a stacked set; dimensions, materials and production details need confirmation for the actual product.

List every bottle, vial, cap, card and accessory. Measure the filled product with its closure fitted, note the weight and label orientation, and provide drawings or physical units. A nominal volume does not describe a bottle’s shoulder, cap height or fragile decoration. Keep the top and bottom layer identified on the drawing so the packer and recipient follow the same sequence.
Decide how the second layer is revealed

In a stacked arrangement, the recipient must be able to reach the lower tray without tipping the first one. Try a finger recess, a pull ribbon or a removable upper tray, then verify the chosen feature against the actual load. A pull tab needs an attachment that the intended handling can withstand; its visual presence alone does not establish strength.

Compare the opening on a loaded prototype. Check that fingers can reach the tray without pressing the bottle, the top tray can be set down stably, and the lower items remain visible and accessible. Leave enough working room around closures and labels, but do not specify a universal clearance before measuring the products and material build.
Separate presentation fit from transport protection

Questions to resolve before approving a layered set
PartDecision to documentSample review
Bottle trayProduct orientation and supported contact areasCap clearance, finish contact and removal access
Vial trayNumber, spacing and orientation of each vialLabel visibility and ability to remove one vial at a time
Layer interfaceHow the upper tray locates and liftsNo unintended pressure on lower contents; stable handling
Outer coverLift-off depth, visual alignment and closing methodClosed clearance and repeatable lid fit
Shipping packCarton, packing orientation and distribution routeAgreed assessment with actual filled contents

A tight-looking cavity is not proof of retention in transit. Review a paperboard or other insert on the basis of the product’s geometry, contact surfaces and removal needs; compare alternatives in the perfume insert guide. ISTA explains that transport procedures evaluate a complete product-and-package system rather than certifying an individual material.[1] Agree suitable acceptance criteria and a representative distribution route with the relevant parties.
Measure the layers before final artwork

Record the usable inside width and length for each tray, the height of the tallest filled item and the space occupied by tray walls, supports and the cover. Check the complete section rather than adding a nominal bottle height to a nominal vial height. The upper tray, lower tray and cover may each add layers at different points.

As a simple illustration, if measured clear heights for the upper contents and lower contents are 55 mm and 25 mm, their sum is 80 mm before tray bases, lid engagement and project-specific clearance. It is not an external box dimension. Confirm the layered section with a supplier drawing and a physical sample. The inside and outside measurement guide explains why the two dimensions differ.
Compare quotes on the same packed set

Ask each supplier to identify the cover, base, two trays, insert materials, decoration, assembly and any pull feature. Separate sampling and tooling from repeat-order unit pricing and state quantity per design. If the supplier delivers the trays flat or preassembled, include the packing work and storage impact in the comparison. Confirm the final outer carton dimensions, units per carton, gross weight and freight terms before comparing freight quotes.

The existing discovery-set guide addresses selecting and arranging multiple small vials; this guide focuses on a full-size bottle above a separate lower layer and the access and fit between those layers. Use the sampling guide to document revisions and approvals.

1. ISTA: Can I certify an individual packaging material? Reviewed 10 November 2026. The guidance concerns packaged-product testing; it does not establish that this concept or any proposed shipment has been tested.
  2. ISTA: Getting started with design and testing. Reviewed 10 November 2026. Distribution conditions and acceptance criteria depend on the actual product and route.
